title: Launch Sprint: Needle Metrics & Readiness Checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact operational playbook for a 2-week launch sprint focused on "needle metrics"—the tight set of leading indicators that move quickly and reliably when user experience shifts. Use this as the canonical preflight checklist across Product, Engineering, SRE, and CS before any staged release.

How to use this doc:
- Owners fill their rows in the morning stand on D-7, update daily until D+3.
- If any red item persists >12 hours, escalate to the launch commander and pause rollout.
- This is intentionally opinionated: keep the needle set small (4–7 metrics) and actionable.

Needle metrics (primary set) — one-line definitions + thresholds
1) Request P95 latency (production traffic, 99th token) — threshold: <= 350ms (green), 350–650ms (amber), >650ms (red)
2) Error rate (API-level 5xx + timeouts) — threshold: <=0.2% (green), 0.2–1.0% (amber), >1.0% (red)
3) Unit cost (USD per 1k tokens served, rolling 24h) — threshold: <= $0.18 (green), $0.18–$0.30 (amber), >$0.30 (red)
4) Prompt fidelity pass rate (sampled evals, 500 queries/day) — threshold: >= 96% (green), 92–96% (amber), <92% (red)
5) Active user conversion (first-successful-response / first-100 interactions) — threshold: >= 8% (green), 5–8% (amber), <5% (red)
6) KV cache hit rate (for cached prefixes) — threshold: >= 62% (green), 45–62% (amber), <45% (red)
7) Canary rollback count (per hour) — threshold: 0 recommended, >0 escalate immediately

Secondary probes (fast lightweight signals) — not block but informative:
- Tail memory pressure on GPUs (top node value) — spike >85% -> alert SRE
- Queue depth > 40 at peak batching window -> consider throttling
- Function-calling failures (tooling integration) >0.5% -> notify solutions engineering

Owners table (copy to the master sheet and fill):
- Product owner: Maya Thompson — overall go/no-go and user-facing tradeoffs
- Release lead / commander: Liam Chen — orchestration, traffic shifts, CLI
- SRE / Observability: Rosa Alvarez — alerts, dashboards, tracing, postmortem
- Serving runtime eng: Ethan Patel — kernel/quant config, batching, memory knobs
- QA / Eval lead: Priya Nair — prompt fidelity sampling and regression triage
- CS / Beta customers: Daniel Wu — customer comms, escalations, pilot invites

Daily preflight checklist (D-7 -> D-1):
- D-7: Smoke deploy in stage with representative traffic (20% sample). Verify P95 and error rate.
- D-6: Run 1k sampled fidelity prompts against new model + holdback model; attach diff notes.
- D-5: Billing/cost projection for expected 7-day flight; validate burst plan for Dedicated pools.
- D-4: Security review complete for model and third-party artifacts; KMS keys rotation validated.
- D-3: Observability gaps filled: tracing hooks for token-level spans, sampling tags for experiment id.
- D-2: Canary orchestration pilot on 1% traffic; automated rollback test exercised.
- D-1: Stakeholder readout; go/no-go dry run and comms template approved.

Go / No-go decision heuristic (D-1 final):
- Green: All primary needle metrics green for 24h on canary + no open P1/P0 incidents -> GO
- Amber: One amber but with clear mitigation, SRE signoff, and rollback plan documented -> conditional GO with tight monitoring
- Red: Any primary metric in red or >2 ambers -> NO-GO (pause rollout, investigate)

Rollout plan (traffic shift cadence):
- Canary 1: 0.5% traffic for 4 hours. Check needles every 15 min.
- Canary 2: 2% for 3 hours. Check + run sampled fidelity.
- Ramp 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 1–2h steady windows; abort on sustained red
- Autoscaling: Dedicated pools may pre-warm extra nodes at 25% step; confirm billing watch is active

Contingencies and quick remediation recipes:
- Latency spike (P95 > 650ms): throttle batching (reduce max batch size), fall back to lower-precision quantized model, switch to lower-cost region if routing policy permits
- Error surge (5xx > 1%): redirect traffic to fallback model variant, disable new feature flags, increase timeouts then roll back release if errors not resolved in 30m
- Cost drift (> +40% expected): engage finance, enable cost throttle (cap tokens/min per API key), pause non-critical background jobs
- Fidelity regression: revert to previous model version or enable prompt prompt-templating patch; run emergency eval set and isolate root-cause (tokenization change, truncation, prompt drift)

Observability playbook (must-haves pre-launch):
- Dashboard: single-pane view with needle metrics + per-region split (P95, errors, cost, fidelity, kv-hit)
- Alerting: severity-tied channels and runbooks (PagerDuty for red, Slack channel for amber)
- Traces: end-to-end spans including request-routing decision, model-variant id, quantization profile tag
- Sampled logs: attach 100 example prompt-responses to fidelity dashboard every 6h

Customer comms template (to be copied into CS):
- Subject: Beta launch: [feature] — what to expect; brief rollback window and contact
- Body bullets: brief feature description, expected availability, known limitations, support channel, escalation contact

Post-launch 72h runbook (D+0 -> D+3):
- D+0 first 6h: hourly checkpoint meetings between Release lead, SRE, Product; compile hot-fix list
- D+1: escalate any fidelity regression items to applied-ml with priority tags; confirm cost vs forecast
- D+2: evaluate user metrics vs cohort baseline (conversion, retention, errors by customer)
- D+3: decision: full rollout confirmed vs rollback initiated; if full rollout, schedule 7-day watch and retrospective

Retention of artifacts (who does what after launch):
- SRE: create incident postmortem for any Sev>2 within 72h
- Product: create feature adoption brief with top 10 qualitative issues from CS
- Eng: land any immediate patch PRs within 48h and tag for follow-up roadmap items

Open questions / Risks (notes to resolve during D-7):
- Are there any outstanding model-licensing constraints for private deployments? (owner: legal, ETA D-5)
- Is the dedicated pool quota secured for the expected traffic spike? (owner: infra, ETA D-6)
- Do we have a validated fallback model variant with acceptable latency for user-facing flows? (owner: serving-runtime, ETA D-4)

Appendix — quick copies:
- Canary check snapshot command: curl -H 'X-Experiment: newmodel' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?sample=1 | jq '.latency,.status'
- Fidelity sampling script: scripts/eval/sample_and_diff.sh --seed-file sample_prompts.txt --target newmodel --reference stablemodel --out diffs.csv

Notes (working):
- This doc intentionally biases toward short feedback loops; if you need more detailed KPI spreadsheets, link back to the product-ops KPI ledger (Confluence).
- Keep the needle metric set stable across releases so trends are comparable.

Last updated: 2025-03-04 by Maya Thompson
